title: Tools, access equipment and manual tasks
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: WorkSafe Victoria, High risk work licence (reviewed 30 June 2026); SafeWork NSW, High risk work licences (last modified 15 June 2026; no visible date); WorkSafe Queensland, Boom type elevating work platform (WP) (no date shown).
audience: Property manager partner workers who use tools, access equipment and carry or move loads
learningOutcomes: Check tools and access equipment for defects, and tag out any that are unsafe.
Plan load handling and manual tasks so that improvisation is avoided.
Refuse to proceed when access or equipment is unsafe, and record the decision.

instruction.heading: Check the equipment before it is used
instruction.body: Check every tool and item of access equipment before the job, and at the start of each day. A drill with a frayed cable is not safe to use, and it must be tagged out. A ladder with a cracked rail or a missing foot is not safe to climb. Record defects, tag out what is unsafe, and remove it from the work area. Do not use a damaged item because it is needed for a small task.

instruction.heading: Plan access and manual handling
instruction.body: Choose the access method before the task, not after. A proposal to use a ladder on uneven ground should lead to a different method, not to a compromise. For manual handling, plan the route, the weight and the number of people needed. Use a trolley or a mechanical aid where the load is heavy or awkward. Share a heavy lift with another person when the load requires it, and set the load down rather than twisting while holding it. Ergonomic load management prevents strain injuries in tasks that look light but are repeated.

instruction.heading: Refuse unsafe conditions
instruction.body: The job does not proceed merely because the repair appears brief. If the equipment is unsafe, the access is unsafe, or the load cannot be moved safely, stop and record the decision. Tell the approver the reason and the alternative method needed. A refusal recorded with a reason protects the worker and gives the owner a clear next step.

procedure: Inspect each tool and piece of access equipment before the job and at the start of each day.
Tag out and remove any defective item, and record it.
Plan the access method and the route for any load before starting.
Use a trolley or mechanical aid for heavy or awkward loads, and share the lift where needed.
Refuse unsafe access or equipment, and record the reason and the alternative.
Record the equipment checks and any refusal.

workedExamples.situation: A portable drill has a frayed cable, and the technician proposes using a ladder on uneven ground to reach the task.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should happen to the drill and to the proposed ladder use?
workedExamples.reasoning: Tag out and isolate the drill, because the frayed cable is a defect. Do not use the ladder on uneven ground. Choose a safer access method, such as a platform set up for the task, and plan the load handling. Record the defect and the refusal, and tell the approver what is needed before the task can continue.

equipmentAndPpe: Trolley, sack truck or mechanical aid for heavy loads
Safety footwear and gloves suited to the load

commonErrors.error: Using a damaged tool because it is needed for a small job.
commonErrors.prevention: Tag out the damaged tool and get a sound one.

commonErrors.error: Improvising access with a chair, a box or a stack of items.
commonErrors.prevention: Choose a designed access method. Refuse improvised access.

commonErrors.error: Lifting a heavy load alone and twisting while holding it.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a trolley or share the lift, and set the load down before turning.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Use of ladders and elevated access is subject to “Ladders, elevated access and fall prevention”. A boom-type elevating work platform needs the WP licence where the boom is 11 metres or more in New South Wales and Queensland (SafeWork NSW licence page; WorkSafe Queensland page). A shorter boom may not need the licence in those states. Victoria's WP class page gives no boom length (reviewed 30 June 2026), so the Victorian licence is not limited by length. Work above the threshold needs the licence. This lesson does not grant it.
Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or authority to operate plant or to perform regulated work.

qualityStandard: Every tool and access item is checked before use, and the check is recorded.
No improvised access is used, and every load is planned before it is moved.
Every refusal is recorded with the reason and the alternative.
documentationEvidence: Daily equipment check record with any defective item tagged out
Access and load-handling plan for the job
summary: Check tools and access equipment before use, and tag out defects.
Choose the access method and plan the load before starting.
Refuse unsafe conditions and record the refusal and the alternative.

knowledgeChecks.question: A drill has a frayed cable and a ladder is proposed on uneven ground. What is correct?
options: Use the drill carefully and the ladder on the uneven ground, since the ground is firm enough today
Tape the cable and continue the job, since the tape will hold the wire in place for the day
Use the drill but not the ladder, since the drill is fine with the frayed cable on it
Tag out the drill, do not use the ladder on uneven ground, and choose a safer access method

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a heavy load be moved?
options: With a trolley or a mechanical aid, or shared between two people, after the route is planned
Alone and quickly, since the load is not that heavy for one person to lift in one go
By twisting while holding it, since that is the quickest way to shift it across the floor
By carrying it up a ladder, since the route is shorter that way than the stairs

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say to record when a job is refused because the equipment or access is unsafe?
options: Nothing, the job simply does not proceed
The decision, the reason, and the alternative method needed
Only the start time of the visit
The worker's personal view of the owner
